stem: In the figure, \(AB = AC\) and the measure of angle \(ABC\) is \(34^{\circ}\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: Because \(AB = AC\), the angles opposite these sides are equal: angle \(ACB\) = angle \(ABC = 34^{\circ}\).
The angles of the triangle add up to \(180^{\circ}\): \(x + 34 + 34 = 180\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{180 - 34}{2}\), which treats the 34° angle as the angle between the equal sides. The 34° angle is at \(B\), one of the two equal base angles.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 34\), which subtracts only one of the two 34° base angles.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This assumes all three angles are equal. Only the two angles opposite the equal sides, \(B\) and \(C\), are equal.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(d('A','B')-d('A','C'))<0.01 and abs(ang('A','B','C')-34)<0.1
ans=180-2*34
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
